title: The Siege of Chittor
historical_context: Chittor was the principal stronghold of Mewar and came under siege by Mughal forces led by Akbar in late 1567.
The defence of the fort is associated with commanders including Jaimal Rathore and Patta Chundawat after Udai Singh II withdrew from the final defence.
Mughal siege operations included covered approaches (sabats) and mining/siege engineering.
The fort fell to Mughal forces in February 1568 after a prolonged siege.

state_variables.label: Food Stores
state_variables.description: Garrison food supplies. Depletion causes morale and manpower loss.

state_variables.label: Water Supply
state_variables.description: Fortress water reserves. Critical for survival under siege.

state_variables.label: Defenders
state_variables.description: Normalized manpower index of the garrison. Loss weakens all defences.

state_variables.label: Morale
state_variables.description: Garrison and civilian morale. Affected by resources, losses, and decisions.

state_variables.label: Fort Integrity
state_variables.description: Structural condition of the fort's defences. Degraded by siege engineering.

state_variables.label: Siege Progress
state_variables.description: Mughal siege advancement. Higher values are worse for defenders.

decision_points.prompt: The siege works are advancing. What should the defenders prioritize?

options.title: Concentrate Defenders
options.description: Commit more defenders to the most threatened approaches.

options.title: Reinforce Sectors
options.description: Strengthen threatened positions while preserving more of the garrison.

options.title: Limited Sortie
options.description: Attempt a focused counteraction against nearby siege activity.

options.title: Conserve Strength
options.description: Accept slower pressure now to preserve the garrison for later turns.

decision_points.prompt: A major defensive sector is under severe pressure. How do you respond?
decision_points.trigger_condition: Reach turn 3, or fort_integrity <= 55, or siege_progress >= 60

options.title: Concentrate at Breach
options.description: Commit remaining strength to the most threatened defensive point.

options.title: Redistribute Defenders
options.description: Spread the remaining force across several critical positions.

options.title: Counterattack Siege Works
options.description: Attempt another direct disruption of the siege operation.

options.title: Preserve Remaining Strength
options.description: Reduce immediate losses even if the fort's position worsens.

canonical_timeline.title: Mughal siege begins
canonical_timeline.description: Akbar leads the Mughal campaign against Chittor and the fort comes under siege.

canonical_timeline.title: Siege works advance
canonical_timeline.description: Accounts describe covered approaches and mining/siege engineering used against the fort.

canonical_timeline.title: Jaimal is killed
canonical_timeline.description: Abu'l Fazl and Badayuni describe Jaimal being shot during the final stage of the siege; the V&A Akbarnama manuscript also depicts this episode.

canonical_timeline.title: Chittor falls
canonical_timeline.description: The fort is captured by Mughal forces after the prolonged siege.

historical_constraints.title: No external relief force
historical_constraints.description: No documented external Rajput relief force arrived to break the Mughal siege during the period.

historical_constraints.title: Mughal siege engineering
historical_constraints.description: Mughal forces used covered approaches (sabats) and mining operations, providing persistent siege pressure.

historical_constraints.title: Limited water sources
historical_constraints.description: The fort's water supplies were finite and could not be resupplied during the siege.

historical_constraints.title: Finite food stores
historical_constraints.description: The garrison's food reserves depleted over the months-long siege with no resupply route.

fictional_composites.rationale: No single named Mughal siege engineer is identified in the primary sources used by this project. This composite represents the documented Mughal siege-engineering capability.
No single named civilian logistics officer is identified in the sources. This composite represents the documented civilian and logistics perspective within the fort.

simulation_notes.content: All numerical state values (food, water, defenders, morale, fort_integrity, siege_progress) are gameplay abstractions on a 0–100 scale. They are not historical measurements.
Choice deltas and passive turn effects are authored counterfactual game mechanics, not claims about exact historical rates or quantities.
The simulation is fully deterministic in the MVP: same starting state plus same choices always produces the same outcome. No randomness is used.
Threshold rules (e.g., food < 30 triggers morale penalty) are gameplay design to create meaningful consequences, not historical claims about specific breakpoints.

evidence.claim: Abu'l Fazl's Akbarnama contains an account of Akbar's siege of Chittor.
evidence.source: Abu'l Fazl, Akbarnama, Chittor siege account
evidence.note: Use a reliable edition/translation for final in-game citations.

evidence.claim: Badayuni's Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh gives a contrasting/parallel account of the final stage of the siege and Jaimal's death.
evidence.note: Historical narratives should be attributed where interpretations differ.

evidence.claim: Modern scholarly synthesis discusses the Chittor campaign and siege as part of Akbar's Mughal expansion.
evidence.source: Satish Chandra, Medieval India: From Sultanat to the Mughals, Part II
evidence.note: Use the relevant edition/page citation in the final build.

evidence.claim: Modern scholarship on Mewar provides historical context for the Chittor siege.
evidence.source: R. V. Somani, History of Mewar, from Earliest Times to 1751 A.D.
evidence.note: Use the relevant edition/page citation in the final build.

evidence.claim: A Victoria and Albert Museum Akbarnama manuscript scene depicts Akbar shooting Jaimal during the siege.
evidence.source: Victoria and Albert Museum, Akbarnama manuscript record
evidence.note: The artwork is a later manuscript illustration of the event, not a photograph or eyewitness image.

evidence.claim: State deltas and player outcomes are counterfactual gameplay mechanics.
evidence.note: Never present these numerical effects as historical measurements.
